metadata.title: Mason Taylor - Green light to return for Week 5
metadata.description: Taylor (thumb) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Browns, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Taylor strung together a trio of full practices, and the second-year rookie has been cleared to return Sunday from a two-game absence due to a thumb injury. He saw just three targets through the first two games of the regular season, whereas rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq has turned 18 targets from QB Geno Smith into a 12-143-1 receiving line across four games. That said, both of the Jets tight ends could find success against a Browns defense that ranks in the bottom-10 in the league in fantasy points allowed to tight ends.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor (thumb) to return Sunday
metadata.description: Mason Taylor (thumb) will be active for Sunday's game against the Browns.
metadata.analysis: Taylor has missed each of the last two weeks due to a thumb injury, but the second-year TE will be back for Sunday's game. Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods figure to see fewer snaps as a result.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor (thumb) logs full practice Wednesday

metadata.title: Mason Taylor - Churns out full practice
metadata.description: Taylor (thumb) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Taylor didn't practice in any fashion and sat out for both of the Jets' past two games due to the thumb injury, but he appears to be close to 100 percent ahead of Sunday's contest against the Browns after operating with no restrictions to kick off Week 5 prep. The second-year tight end paced Jets tight ends in snaps through the first two weeks of the season, but he may have to settle for a lesser role upon his return. Rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq -- who handled light workloads the first two weeks after missing much of training camp and the preseason while recovering from hernia surgery -- has seen his snap counts ramp up over the past two weeks while Taylor was sidelined and produced a 7-105-1 receiving line on 12 targets during that stretch. Sadiq now looks poised to operate as the Jets' top option at tight end ahead of Taylor moving forward.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor (thumb) cleared to return to practice

metadata.title: Mason Taylor - Back at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Taylor (thumb) will practice Wednesday, Eric Allen of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Taylor has missed the past two games with his thumb issue, but his involvement in practice to kick off Week 5 prep gives him a good chance at playing Sunday versus the Browns. Though he led Jets tight ends in snaps in the team's first two games before missing time with the injury, Taylor is expected to take more of a back seat behind rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq upon returning to action. After undergoing hernia surgery during the offseason, Sadiq missed considerable practice time during training camp and was eased in with a small role to begin the season, but he's emerged as a key part of the passing game over the past two weeks with a combined 7-105-1 receiving line on 12 targets.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor Deemed Out for Second Straight Game
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) has been ruled out for Sunday's road game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field. It's no surprise that the 22-year-old will miss a second straight appearance after not practicing since injuring his thumb in the team's 20-17 loss to the Packers in Week 2. The trio of Kenyon Sadiq, Jeremy Ruckert, and Jelani Woods will again divvy up the snaps with the second-year pro set to be inactive. It will be interesting to see how the snap share shakes out when Taylor returns to action. When healthy, he led the room by a solid margin, though that could change if Sadiq's Week 3 breakout weren't a fluke.

metadata.description: Mason Taylor (thumb) will not play in Sunday's game against the Bears.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor Ruled Out for Week 3
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Detroit, according to Rich Cimini. Taylor suffered the injury in last week's loss to Green Bay and was considered week-to-week entering Week 3. He did not practice Wednesday or Thursday before being ruled out Friday. Taylor has two catches for minus-two yards through the first two weeks and did not record a reception against the Packers. His absence leaves rookie Kenyon Sadiq and Jeremy Ruckert as the Jets' primary options at tight end. Sadiq caught two passes for 17 yards last week, while Ruckert finished with two catches for five yards.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor - Likely out for Week 3
metadata.description: Taylor (thumb) is considered week-to-week and will likely miss Sunday's game against the Lions, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Taylor exited Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers due to the thumb issue and doesn't look like he'll be able to practice in any fashion Week 3 while he recovers from the injury. Though Taylor was on the field for about two-thirds of the Jets' offensive snaps in the Week 1 win over the Titans, he had been expected to see his playing time get gradually scaled back once rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq regained full conditioning after missing most of training camp and the preseason due to a hernia. Taylor's expected absence against Detroit should clear the way for Sadiq to see his largest share of playing time to date, and Jeremy Ruckert could also benefit from an expanded role at tight end.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor Likely to Miss Week 3 With Thumb Injury
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Mason Taylor (thumb), who suffered a thumb injury in the Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers, is considered week-to-week and is likely to miss the Week 3 contest this weekend against the Detroit Lions, sources told Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. The 22-year-old former second-rounder last year from LSU caught 44 of 65 targets for 369 yards and only one touchdown in 13 games as a rookie in a bad Jets offense, and he was expected to eventually take a back seat this year to first-rounder Kenyon Sadiq, who missed much of training camp following hernia surgery. When Taylor returns from his thumb injury, there is a good chance he will see his role shrink behind Sadiq. Taylor has only two receptions on three targets for minus-two yards through the first two weeks of his sophomore campaign. Sadiq, who is rostered in only 18% of Yahoo leagues, should become more attractive on the waiver wire this week with Taylor now banged up. The 21-year-old from Oregon is an elite athlete with more downfield pass-catching prowess and versatility. He already has five catches for 38 yards and has run in a touchdown in his first two NFL games.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor - Iffy to return due to thumb injury
metadata.description: Taylor (thumb) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Packers, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Taylor appeared to have picked up the thumb injury during the second half or overtime and is questionable to return. Rookie first-rounder Kenyon Sadiq will serve as the Jets' TE1 for as long as Taylor is out of the game, with Jeremy Ruckert and Andrew Beck providing depth at the position.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor Injures Thumb, Doesn't Get On Stat Sheet in Week 2 Loss
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) exited Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers after sustaining an injury and failing to make it on the stat sheet. The second-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft left Sunday's game late, and it is unclear what play he was injured on. Meanwhile, rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq had two catches for 17 yards in Sunday's effort, and wide receiver Garrett Wilson caught the receiving corps' only passing touchdown of the day. It is unclear whether Taylor will miss any time, though fantasy managers have surely moved on already given his lack of production.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor's Role Not Translating to Fantasy Value
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Mason Taylor earned the start in Week 1 and played 66% of the offensive snaps, but he turned in a very lackluster performance from a fantasy football perspective. He caught just two of his three targets for minus-two yards, which indicates that he spent most of the game blocking or serving as a security blanket near the line of scrimmage. Indeed, he had a miserable average depth of target of 0.3 yards in the season opener. All the while, rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq caught three passes for 21 yards and had a rushing touchdown, despite playing less than half of the offensive snaps. All signs point to Sadiq easing his way into the starting tight end role within the next few weeks, which will drop Taylor further down the depth chart. The 22-year-old can be avoided in fantasy football as long as Sadiq is healthy.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor - Minimal production in Week 1
metadata.description: Taylor caught two of three targets for minus-2 yards in the Jets' 23-10 win over the Titans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Taylor got the start at tight end and played 44 of 67 offensive snaps. He ran 16 routes on Geno Smith's 26 dropbacks but had a laughable zero-yard average depth of target, giving him no chance to produce much in the box score. Taylor has next to no fantasy value in the Jets' low-volume passing offense that will feature Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall first and foremost.

metadata.title: Mason Taylor Faces Crowded Tight End Picture in Week 1
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Mason Taylor enters his second season after catching 44 of 65 targets for 369 yards and one touchdown across 13 games as a rookie. Taylor remains in position to start, but the Jets added first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq and still have Jeremy Ruckert in the rotation. Sadiq practiced fully this week after dealing with a groin injury, giving New York another athletic option in the passing game. Garrett Wilson's return also restores the clear top target for new quarterback Geno Smith. Taylor averaged only 8.4 yards per reception last season, so he needs either more volume or more scoring opportunities to become a dependable fantasy option. RotoBaller ranks Taylor TE42 for Week 1. He is best left out of standard lineups, including most two-tight-end formats, until the Jets show how the routes and targets will be divided.
